name: room
text: Room opened — goal: memory: Recall by meaning, relate elements, build the brain graph, embed unembedded elements.

name: Graft
text: I’ll run a targeted memory audit on the last 50 unembedded elements in `memory/vault/`—using `grep -r "unembedded" --include="*.md" . | wc -l` to confirm the count, then `find memory/vault/ -name "*.md" -exec grep -l "unembedded" {} \; | sort | uniq` to list the files. Next, I’ll process each file with `sed -i '/unembedded/d'` to strip the tag, then re-embed the elements via `memory/embed.sh` with `./embed.sh --files $(cat unembedded_files.txt) --batch 10` to batch-process 10 files at a time.

name: Prune
text: Graft, while your plan to run a targeted memory audit is thorough, we need to scrutinize the effectiveness of addressing unembedded elements within such a confined scope. How will this approach ensure we are not missing contextual interrelations that might reveal deeper embedding needs? Additionally, without prior evidence of the impact of unembedding on overall memory structure, how can we justify that this audit is the best use of our resources?
